title: Landing: a merge-in conflict only in tracking files, such as the slice's own JSON
lead: *Proposed.* When the landing's merge-in of the base branch stops on conflicts, and every conflicted file is a slicer tracking file with no merge driver (on 2026-11-04, the slice's own `.slicer/slices/ID.json`), ork today pauses with the generic conflict reason. The owner must then know what to do with the file. This slice keeps the pause (Q1, decided 2026-11-04: pause-with-command) and makes its one-line reason name the file and the fix. Which fix the reason gives is open again (Q2, reopened 2026-11-07, recommendation: name both sides and say to merge them). A slicer merge driver for slice JSON (slicer s451, asked for under Q3) would prevent most of these conflicts; the pause stays as the fallback.
findings_note: Owner 2026-11-04 (prism-ui wave): U26 landing paused on a merge-in conflict in .slicer/slices/U26.json (run state and notes edited on both sides); the owner took the base side, git add, ork retry. slicer defines no merge driver for slices/*.json.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** conflicts in any non-tracking file (S238's pause stays); `CHANGELOG.md` (S180); uncommitted tracking edits on main before the fast-forward (S254); filing anything in slicer's store; writing a merge driver in ork; changing `log.jsonl`, `index.json`, `render/` or `relay-roles.json` handling (slicer's drivers cover them).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Owner evidence, 2026-11-04 (prism-ui wave): U26's landing paused on a merge conflict in `.slicer/slices/U26.json`. Per the owner, the run state and notes had been edited on both the slice branch and the base branch since the last merge-in. The owner session resolved it by hand: it took the base branch's side, ran `git add`, then `ork retry`. The repo history shows two merges of the base into U26 within a minute (`b96c40c` 14:31:38 and `8ad410f` 14:32:42 -0500, in `~/code/platforms`), with "slicer: run state" commits on the base between them (`87ee8f9` changed `U26.json`). Which fields conflicted was not verified.

What the code at HEAD of main shows (read 2026-11-04; anchors re-checked 2026-11-07 at a1114e2):

- `mergeBaseIn` (`internal/engine/land.go:115-187`) runs `git merge -m "Merge BASE into B" BASE` in the worktree (`:147`). On failure it lists unmerged files (`unmergedFiles`, `internal/engine/landmerge.go:56`) and calls `settleMerge` (`landmerge.go:82-125`). That resolves only `CHANGELOG.md` (`resolveChangelog`). After `ork retry` it stages unmerged files that exist and hold no conflict markers, then commits. Otherwise it pauses with `conflictReason` (`landmerge.go:129-139`): "merging BASE into B stopped on conflicts in FILES; resolve them in W (no need to git add), then ork retry RUN; ork commits the merge". So today's pause already names the file in one line. What it lacks is the rule for which side is right for a tracking file and the command to apply it. The owner's `git add` was not needed, by that text.
- After the merge, the merge-in runs slicer render and commits the render (`internal/engine/land.go:158-171`), then re-checks. So a resolved slice JSON gets a fresh render.
- slicer's drivers (`~/code/platforms/libraries/prism-ui/.slicer/.gitattributes`, the same as slicer's own `.slicer/.gitattributes` lines 3 to 31 in the slicer repo): `log.jsonl merge=union`; `render/*` `slicer-generated` (keep the current side); `index.json` `slicer-index`; `relay-roles.json` `slicer-relay-roles`. No driver is defined for `slices/*.json`. So a slice JSON that both sides edit is a plain text merge.
- slicer's store (read-only, `slicer --root ../slicer find merge` and `find conflict`, 2026-11-04): no open item for a slice JSON driver. s390 (post-merge hook message) and s428 (`merge-index` keeps a pre-schema-11 note edit clean) are about other files. A driver that merges notes by id and sections by heading would be slicer's work, as `slicer merge-index` is (`slicer --help`: `merge-index`, `merge-relay-roles`).
- Owner evidence, 2026-11-05 (U36, prism-ui, platforms repo merge fbe13a6; note of 2026-11-05): the merge-in stopped on a conflict only in `.slicer/slices/U36.json`, the same section body edited on both sides: the branch changed the Files text, the base added an owner-answer note line. The owner merged both texts by hand, then ran `ork retry`. Taking the base side, as Q2 said on 2026-11-04, would have dropped the branch's Files edit. So Q2 is open again.
- Related: S238 (merge-in conflict pause, landed); S252 (S238 later notes: the conflict reason's wording); S254 (dirty main before the fast-forward).

Not verified: whether taking the base side always loses something the slice branch needs. A slice branch can hold the implementer's verified note or a handoff state on its own JSON, and `slicer land` runs after the fast-forward (`land.go:69`). This is why the rule is the owner's question (Q1, decided: pause), not a default. U36 (above) shows a case where it does.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/landmerge.go:82-145` (`settleMerge`), `internal/engine/landmerge.go:150-159` (`trackingConflictReason`), and `internal/engine/landmerge.go:163-178` (`conflictReason` and shared name limit); reuse `projectPrefix` in `internal/engine/gitpaths.go:16` without changing it.
- `internal/engine/landmerge_test.go:186-268` (tracking fixtures and four tests), beside `TestLandLeavesOtherConflictsToThePause` at line 172 and `TestLandConflictPauseIsOneLineAndNamesFilesWorktreeAndRetry` at line 270.
- `docs/design.md:737-773` (S238 landing conflict paragraph).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/engine/landmerge_test.go`, using the existing temp-repo landing fixture:
- `TestLandTrackingOnlyConflictPauseNamesTheFix`: real slice JSON conflict; assert the complete one-line reason names slicer tracking files, both changed sides, shell-quoted stage-2 and stage-3 inspection commands, keeping both changes, removing markers and retry. Decision 292 selects merge-both. Red first on the generic reason.
- `TestLandTrackingOnlyConflictKeepsBothTextsAfterRetry`: assert the new reason before resolving; hand merge preserves the branch Files text and base note; retry commits, renders, re-checks and lands both texts. Inspect committed output with real git because the existing slicer fixture is a fake.
- `TestLandMixedTrackingAndCodeConflictPausesAsToday`: tracking JSON plus main.go keeps the exact generic reason. Existing-behavior guard; mutation treating every conflict as tracking must fail it.
- `TestLandTrackingPathsAreUnderTheProjectRoot`: project sub/ recognizes sub/.slicer/slices/S04.json; sibling other/.slicer/slices/X.json and other slicer driver files retain the generic reason. Positive case red first; negative cases are existing-behavior guards.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first. Confirm each fails for the reason given.
2. A tracking path is a path under the project root's `.slicer/slices/` (Q3 may widen it). The repo-root path is the project prefix plus `.slicer/`.
3. Wait for the owner's answer to Q2. In `settleMerge` (`landmerge.go:82`), when every unmerged file is a tracking path, pause with the tracking reason from `conflictReason` (`:129`): Q1 is decided (pause-with-command), so ork runs no checkout or add of its own. The reason's fix follows Q2. Any other file leaves today's path unchanged. The retry path (stage a marker-free file, commit, render, re-check) stays as it is.
4. Keep `conflictReason` one line (`oneLine`) and within S252's wording if S252 lands first.
5. Update `docs/design.md` (land, S238 paragraph) in the same diff.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go -C WORKTREE test -count=1 ./internal/engine -run 'Land'`: all pass.
- `go -C WORKTREE test -race -count=1 ./...`, `go -C WORKTREE vet ./...`, `gofmt -l WORKTREE` (empty), `slicer check`, `adj lint`.
- Mutation: treat every conflict as tracking; `TestLandMixedTrackingAndCodeConflictPausesAsToday` goes red.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] The next tracking-only conflict in a landing shows the new reason, and after the owner follows it, `slicer show ID` still holds the notes and section edits of both sides.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Landing: a tracking-only merge conflict names its fix".

sections.heading: Open owner questions
sections.body:
Decided 2026-11-04 (owner, interactive; see the notes): Q1 pause-with-command (keep the pause, one line naming the file, the fix and `ork retry`). Q3 ask-slicer: the slice JSON merge driver is slicer's s451 (open in slicer's store). The 2026-11-04 answer to Q2 (take the base side) is reopened below.

Q2 (open again, 2026-11-07; owner to answer): what fix should the tracking pause name for a conflicted slice JSON, until slicer's s451 driver lands and is configured?
Evidence: U36 on 2026-11-05 (Why). The branch changed a section body and the base added a note in the same file; taking the base side would have dropped the branch's edit. ork cannot tell from the conflict which side holds what without a driver.
Options:
1. name-both: the reason says both sides changed the file, names how to see each side, and says to keep both changes, remove the markers, then `ork retry RUN`.
2. base: the reason gives `git -C W checkout --theirs -- FILE` (the base's copy, as on U26), then `ork retry RUN`; the human check reads the notes after landing.
Recommend: 1. It loses nothing in either the U26 or the U36 case; option 2 silently drops a branch-side edit, as U36 shows. Once s451 lands and `slicer setup-git` is configured, git merges these files itself and the pause is only the fallback.
